q: What is the carbon footprint of a truck body built in Namakkal, and where does it come from?
title: Namakkal truck body footprint
short: Mostly from the steel. A body using 2 tonnes of steel at about 2.3 tonnes CO2 per tonne carries roughly 4.6 tonnes before your own welding, painting and power. Ask steel suppliers for their figure; use an average labelled as an estimate until they reply.
audience: Truck body and trailer builders in Namakkal and Tiruchengode

ul: Steel sheet, sections and tubes by weight, from invoices.
Paint and primer, welding gas and electrodes.
Electricity and diesel used in the shed.

p: Lighter designs with high strength steel cut tonnes per body, and buyers notice lower weight and fuel use.

senseible: Senseible turns supplier invoices into a Scope 3 record with the supplier, quantity and factor behind every figure, so you can see which data is still missing.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard

example.title: Example: one body
lines: 2.0 t steel × 2.3 t CO2/t = 4.6 t CO2
Add your own power, diesel and paint
example.note: 2.3 is an illustrative average for blast furnace steel; replace it with supplier data.
